text: By this test Shakespeare had already been proved. He had outlived his rivals and his patrons; and, when Johnson wrote, nearly a century and a half of changing taste, new manners, and new rules of writing had passed over him, yet had not diminished the delight which he afforded. Johnson gathered the whole result into one image (Johnson 1765): "The stream of time, which is continually washing the dissoluble fabricks of other poets, passes without injury by the adamant of Shakespeare."
